topics.title: Geological Controls on Watershed Carbon and Nitrogen Cycling
topics.question: How does the underlying geology regulate riverine nutrient cycling and greenhouse gas emissions?
paragraphs: We combine catchment-scale field investigations, biogeochemical experiments and global data analysis to examine how rock weathering and lithology shape riverine carbon–nitrogen coupling.

Our work has revealed how carbonate weathering enhances nitrogen assimilatory uptake and how geological settings influence nitrous oxide emission risks. These studies connect processes observed in the Pearl River Basin with broader patterns across river networks.
topics.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of carbonate weathering and riverine nitrogen assimilation
topics.caption: Carbonate weathering and riverine nitrogen uptake. Qi et al., Nature Geoscience (2025).

topics.title: Coastal Groundwater Exchange and Biogeochemical Reactions
topics.question: How do tides, aquifer structure and reactive minerals control the material fluxes entering coastal waters?
paragraphs: We investigate coastal aquifers as reactive interfaces where fresh groundwater and seawater mix. Field monitoring, isotope tracing and laboratory experiments help us connect groundwater flow with nutrient transformations and submarine groundwater discharge.

Current work examines dissolved inorganic nitrogen dynamics, the formation and distribution of iron minerals, and phosphorus retention in permeable sandy beaches. Cheng XING and Yan ZHANG contribute complementary perspectives on hydrological processes and mineral–water interactions.
topics.image_alt: Sandy beach cross-section showing groundwater flow, iron mineral formation and phosphorus retention
topics.caption: Iron cycling and phosphorus retention in a permeable sandy beach. Zhang et al., Chemical Geology (2026).

topics.title: Microplastic Transport from Watersheds to Coastal Estuaries
topics.question: Where do microplastics originate, and what controls their retention, remobilization and delivery to the ocean?
paragraphs: We track microplastic pollution along the land–river–estuary continuum, combining field sampling and particle characterization with spatial analysis of potential sources and transport pathways.

Studies in the Pearl River network and coastal estuaries examine the combined roles of land use, point sources, hydrodynamics and sediment storage. Huan WANG and Xinke LI investigate how these processes affect the movement and fate of microplastics.
topics.image_alt: Conceptual diagram of land-use sources, sediment storage and tidal remobilization of estuarine microplastics
topics.caption: Land use, point sources and tidal regulation of estuarine microplastic transport. Li et al., Journal of Hazardous Materials (2026).

topics.title: Hyporheic Exchange and Riverine Nitrogen Cycling
topics.question: How does exchange between river water, groundwater and riverbed sediments regulate nitrogen retention and removal?
paragraphs: We study the hyporheic zone as a dynamic interface linking groundwater and rivers. The focus is on how exchange pathways and biogeochemical reactions influence the transport, transformation and ecological functions of nitrogen.

Junyi ZHUANG’s work develops this direction through research on hyporheic nitrogen cycling, including a systematic review connecting individual processes with environmental function. Related group studies on carbon fluxes provide a broader context for river–groundwater exchange.
topics.image_alt: Related group study illustrating hyporheic exchange within Pearl River Basin carbon fluxes
topics.caption: Related group work on hyporheic exchange and carbon fluxes. Gu et al., Water Research (2024).

topics.title: Satellite Remote Sensing of Surface-Water Dynamics
topics.question: How can continuous satellite observations reveal the timing and extent of changes in inland water coverage?
paragraphs: Huanglin LUO is developing an approach that combines Harmonized Landsat–Sentinel-2 observations with deep learning to reconstruct monthly, sub-pixel water fraction at 30 m resolution. The aim is to capture gradual changes in water coverage as well as the timing of expansion and contraction.

The research links water-fraction time series with water-body inventories to characterize persistence, seasonality and transitions in rivers, reservoirs and small water bodies. The Greater Bay Area provides the initial study setting.
topics.image_alt: Map of persistent water, seasonal drawdown and highly dynamic transition across the Greater Bay Area study domain
topics.caption: Surface-water dynamic regimes across the Greater Bay Area study domain. Ongoing research by Huanglin LUO.
